claim: The weighted conformal prediction of Tibshirani et al. is described in the supplied abstract as producing distribution-free prediction intervals when test and training covariate distributions differ.
quote: we show that a weighted version of conformal prediction can be used to compute distribution-free prediction intervals for problems in which the test and training covariate distributions differ, but the likelihood ratio between these two distributions is known---or, in practice, can be estimated accurately with access to a large set of unlabeled data (test covariate points).

claim: A secondary source states the marginal guarantee as holding provided the likelihood ratios are exactly known.
quote: The weighted quantile of this distribution yields a prediction set with marginal coverage guarantee P^{test} (Y_{n+1} in C_w(X_{n+1})) >= 1 -alpha, even under covariate shift, provided the likelihood ratios are exactly known.

claim: Gibbs and Candès's related-work summary says that the Tibshirani et al. reweighting approach requires the conditional distribution of Y given X to be constant between training and testing, and the likelihood ratio to be known or very accurately estimated.
quote: However, this requires the conditional distribution of Y |X to be constant between training and testing and the likelihood ratio P 1 (X)/P 0 (X) to be either known or very accurately estimated.

claim: For estimated weights, the supplied sources give only partial coverage. One audit paper says that estimated weighted conformal prediction inherits an approximation term and is not relabeled exact.
quote: oracle test-point WCP has its stated finite-sample guarantee; estimated WCP inherits an approximation term and is not relabeled "exact."
locator: sec. Setting and conformal baselines, para 9

claim: Another source reports that coverage degrades at a rate controlled by the estimation error.
quote: When likelihood ratios must be estimated, coverage degrades at a rate controlled by the estimation error (Barber et al., 2023).

claim: A training-conditional analysis says its results extend to estimated likelihood ratios.
quote: The analysis extends to estimated likelihood ratios and to tail functionals estimated from an unlabeled source sample, which yields a fully finite-sample certificate.

claim: Another paper reports that weighted conformal prediction can undercover substantially when the density ratio is unbounded or must be learned.
quote: it can suffer from significant undercoverage when the density ratio between the distributions is unbounded and/or must be learned.

claim: Barber et al. use weighted quantiles to gain robustness to drift, together with a randomization technique for nonsymmetric algorithms.
quote: we employ weighted quantiles to introduce robustness against distribution drift, and design a new randomization technique to allow for algorithms that do not treat data points symmetrically.

claim: Adaptive conformal inference makes no assumption on the data process: its abstract says it provably achieves the desired coverage frequency over long-time intervals irrespective of the true data generating process.
quote: our adaptive approach provably achieves the desired coverage frequency over long-time intervals irrespective of the true data generating process.

claim: For adaptive conformal inference, the authors state that when the distribution shift is small and the prediction algorithm takes a certain simple form, it will additionally obtain approximate marginal coverage at most time steps.
quote: Moreover, when the distribution shift is small and the prediction algorithm takes a certain simple form we show that ACI will additionally obtain approximate marginal coverage at most time steps.

claim: A later paper notes that ACI requires knowledge of the rate of change of the data-generating mechanism.
quote: unlike ACI, which requires knowledge of the rate of change of the data-generating mechanism, our new procedure is adaptive to both the size and type of the distribution shift.

claim: For f-divergence methods, Cauchois et al. are summarized as valid whenever the two distributions are close in f-divergence.
quote: On the other hand, Cauchois et al. [10] develop methods for forming prediction sets that are valid whenever P 1 and P 0 are close in f -divergence.

claim: The robust validation paper's abstract says its conformal-based method achieves nearly valid coverage in finite samples, under only the condition that the training data be exchangeable.
quote: The method, based on conformal inference, achieves (nearly) valid coverage in finite samples, under only the condition that the training data be exchangeable.

claim: One label-shift paper reports that under stronger shift, all methods incur some coverage loss due to pseudo-label-based density-ratio estimation.
quote: Under stronger shift, all methods incur some coverage loss due to pseudo-label-based density-ratio estimation.

claim: Mixed covariate and conditional shift is also flagged as open, since one source calls simultaneous covariate and label shift with partially identifiable likelihood ratios an open challenge.
quote: Extending the framework to simultaneous covariate and label shift with partially identifiable likelihood ratios is an open challenge.

claim: Under unrestricted conditional shift, one audit paper shows that target coverage is only identified to the full interval from 0 to 1.
quote: a sharp $[0,1]$ identified set for target coverage under unrestricted conditional shift.
